Kimberly / Marissa — draft technical notes below (will be assembled into the DPF evidence pack). Attaching the current evidence pack and a working DPA annex draft for HelixCare review.

[Attachment: redwood_dpf_evidence_pack_v1.pdf (2.4MB)]
[Attachment: dpa_annex_draft_helixcare.docx (45KB)]

Summary of key controls (high-level):
1) Legal & contractual
   - Redwood acts as processor. We provide a standard DPA + optional DPA Annex that maps data categories, subprocessors and transfers. Our DPA incorporates EU SCCs (EC 2021) by reference and includes the UK Addendum for UK personal data.

2) Cross-border transfers / TIA
   - US: We rely on SCCs + technical mitigations. We maintain a documented Transfer Impact Assessment for US-based subprocessors that highlights risk, contractual safeguards, and specific logging/audit capabilities.
   - UK: SCCs + UK Addendum included in the DPA Annex.
   - Australia: We treat as an international transfer; SCCs + contractual safeguards applied; TIA notes specific to state-level requirements included in evidence pack.

3) Subprocessors & data residency
   - Subprocessor list: public/drive link included in the evidence pack. We support: hosted (multi-tenant hosted), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC + on-prem) deployment options.
   - For HelixCare: we can support EU-only processing by offering Dedicated capacity in EU regions or a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). Operational constraints and pricing differ — will include options.

4) Technical measures
   - Encryption at rest: AES-256; in transit: TLS1.3.
   - KV cache and model state: encrypted and ephemeral.
   - KMS/HSM: support for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed key wraps; option to withhold key access from Redwood for customer-supplied keys (subject to feature/config).
   - Access controls: RBAC, SSO, org-scoped API keys, and per-route routing policies.

5) Logging / retention / auditability
   - Operational logs: request metadata and trace IDs retained by default for 90 days.
   - Audit logs: admin changes and security events retained for 7 years for enterprise plans (we can extend retention on request).
   - Data subject / export logs: retained per DPA obligations; we provide log extracts for audits.

6) Telemetry / model usage
   - Model telemetry for quality monitoring can be disabled or limited; we offer options to opt out of prompt/response retention for regulated workloads.

Next steps: assemble a concise DPF evidence PDF, include a redlined DPA Annex tailored to HelixCare, and propose a 30-min call with privacy counsel next week.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side (inline):

> We include SCCs and the UK Addendum by default in the DPA Annex draft.

Can you confirm the UK Addendum text aligns with the UK ICO recommended wording? Would prefer an explicit reference rather than the boilerplate wording.

> If you require EU-only subprocessors, we can offer Dedicated EU-only capacity or Private deployment; I’ve noted the operational points in the annex (service level, backups, and support model).

Can you add a clause that HelixCare may require EU-only subprocessors for specific data categories (PHI) and that Redwood will not engage additional non-EU subprocessors without 30 days notice and an opt-out right?

> Karthik has outlined KMS/HSM and logging options in the evidence pack.

We have a strict retention requirement of 10 years for certain PI categories related to clinical investigations — will Redwood commit to 10 year retention for audit logs tied to those categories? Also need confirmation that customer-managed KMS means HelixCare controls key deletion.

Please mark these as critical redlines; we will share our legal team's suggested edits if helpful. Also, your DocuSign option sounds good — please hold the annex for signature pending our legal redlines.

Thanks,
Elena
